     4	/-!
     5	# Coefficient polynomials and finite-field collision bounds
     6	
     7	This module supplies the coefficient evaluation and polynomial representation
     8	shared by the low-degree games and the combining argument. Distinct bounded
     9	coefficient vectors agree at no more parameters than their degree bound.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	- Blueprint `def:ld-win-predicate` and `lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement`.
    14	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:331-344`.
    15	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element. This is the
    23	representative convention used by the line answers in blueprint
    24	`def:ld-win-predicate`, paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    26	-/
    27	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
    28	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
    29	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
    30	
    31	/-- Interpret a bounded coefficient list as an ordinary univariate
    32	polynomial. This helper makes the line-combination definition use Mathlib's
    33	actual polynomial composition operation. -/
    34	noncomputable def linePolynomialOfCoefficients {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    35	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
    36	  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val
    37	
    38	/-- Evaluating the polynomial represented by a coefficient list agrees with
    39	`evalCoefficient`. -/
    40	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    41	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) (t : K) :
    42	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).eval t = evalCoefficient f t := by
    43	  change Polynomial.eval t
    44	      (∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val) =
    45	    ∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, f i * t ^ i.val
    46	  rw [Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
    47	  simp
    48	
    49	/-- The coefficient polynomial agrees with Mathlib's coefficient-vector
    50	construction. -/
    51	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    52	    [DecidableEq K] {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) :
    53	    linePolynomialOfCoefficients f = Polynomial.ofFn (c + 1) f := by
    54	  simp only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients, Polynomial.ofFn_eq_sum_monomial,
    55	    Polynomial.C_mul_X_pow_eq_monomial]
    56	
    57	/-- Distinct bounded coefficient vectors represent distinct polynomials. -/
    58	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_injective {K : Type*} [Semiring K] (c : ℕ) :
    59	    Function.Injective (linePolynomialOfCoefficients (K := K) (c := c)) := by
    60	  classical
    61	  intro first second heq
    62	  exact Polynomial.injective_ofFn (c + 1)
    63	    (by simpa only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn] using heq)
    64	
    65	/-- The polynomial of a bounded coefficient vector has degree at most `n`. -/
    66	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
    67	    (f : Fin (n + 1) → K) :
    68	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).natDegree ≤ n := by
    69	  classical
    70	  rw [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn]
    71	  exact Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Polynomial.ofFn_natDegree_lt (Nat.succ_pos n) f)
    72	
    73	/-- Distinct coefficient polynomials of degree at most `bound` agree at no
    74	more than `bound` elements of a finite integral domain. This is the univariate
    75	root bound underlying the Schwartz-Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:955`.
    77	No restriction of the degree relative to the field size is required. -/
    78	theorem evalCoefficient_collision_card_le {K : Type*} [CommRing K] [IsDomain K]
    79	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {bound : ℕ}
    80	    (first second : Fin (bound + 1) → K) (hne : first ≠ second) :
    81	    (Finset.univ.filter fun param => evalCoefficient first param =
    82	      evalCoefficient second param).card ≤ bound := by
    83	  classical
    84	  by_contra hcard
    85	  have heq := Polynomial.eq_of_natDegree_lt_card_of_eval_eq'
    86	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients first) (linePolynomialOfCoefficients second)
    87	    (Finset.univ.filter fun param => evalCoefficient first param =
    88	      evalCoefficient second param)
    89	    (fun param hparam => by
    90	      simpa only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval] using (Finset.mem_filter.mp hparam).2)
    91	    (lt_of_le_of_lt (max_le (linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le first)

 /-! ## The `X` block of a truncated extended direction -/
 
 /-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at an `X`-block
 coordinate is the `X` block truncated at that coordinate of the source space.

 `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
 theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)
     (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
     projX (directPointToPauli P
         (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embX P.m i) v)) =
       prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) i (projX (directPointToPauli P v)) := by
   funext a
   change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
       (if (embX P.m a).val < (embX P.m i).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =
     if a.val < i.val then 0 else extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v (embX P.m a))
   rw [embX_val, embX_val]
   by_cases h : a.val < i.val
   · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, map_zero]
   · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]

     projX (directPointToPauli P
       (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embZ P.m i) v)) = 0 := by
   funext a
   have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt

 /-!
 # Self-consistency of the sandwich POVM
 
 The sandwich POVM `R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` of
 `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Sandwich.lean` is approximately self-consistent
 between opposite register placements.  The source establishes this by a
 Cauchy--Schwarz chain (displays `eq:qld-rw-self-cons-1` to
 `eq:qld-rw-self-cons-4`); here an exact identity is used instead.  Writing
 `P_1, P_2` for the two placements of an operator `P`,
 `W_b = (M^Z_b)_1 (M^Z_b)_2`, and `D^W_c = (M^W_c)_1 - (M^W_c)_2`, the
 consistency defect of the two placed sandwiches equals
 `(1/2) ∑_b ‖D^Z_b ψ‖^2 + (1/2) ∑_{a,b} ‖D^X_a W_b ψ‖^2`,
 by two applications of the identity
 `∑_c ⟨w, P_c Q_c w⟩ = ‖w‖^2 - (1/2) ∑_c ‖(P_c - Q_c) w‖^2` for projective
 measurements.  The second sum is then bounded by the self-consistency of `M^X`
 and the commutators on the two placements, since
 `D^X_a W_b = W_b D^X_a + (M^Z_b)_2 K^1_{a,b} - (M^Z_b)_1 K^2_{a,b}`, where
 `K^i_{a,b}` is the placed commutator of `M^X_a` and `M^Z_b`.
 
 ## Main results
 
 * `sandwich_overlap_identity`: the exact expression of the overlap of two
   placed sandwiches.
 * `sandwich_defect_pointwise_le`: the pointwise bound on the consistency
   defect of the sandwich for a fixed point pair.
 * `ProjectiveSetting.sandwichDefectBound`,
   `ProjectiveSetting.sandwich_offDiagonal_le_sandwichDefectBound`, and
   `ProjectiveSetting.avg_sandwichDefectBound_le`: the bound as a function of
   the point pair, the pointwise estimate, and the average.
 
 ## References
 
 Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:743-790`,
 blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:851-880`
 (`lem:qld-4-10`, first step); the identity route is explained in
 `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`.
 -/

 /-- The off-diagonal outcome sum of two complete measurements placed on
 opposite registers is a positive operator.  Formalization-only auxiliary for
 blueprint `def:consistency`, paper
 `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
 theorem offDiagonalPlacedProduct_nonneg {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
     {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
     (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂)
     (M₁ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
     (M₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)) :
     0 ≤ ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
       if a = b then 0
       else S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b) := by
   classical
   have hcomplement : ∀ a : α,
       0 ≤ ∑ b : α, if a = b then (0 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side))
         else M₂.effect b := by
     intro a
     refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => ?_
     by_cases h : a = b
     · rw [if_pos h]
     · rw [if_neg h]
       exact M₂.pos b
   have hrow : ∀ a : α,
       (∑ b : α, if a = b then (0 : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA
           S.toStrategy.ιB))
         else S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)) =
       S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) *
         S.place p₂ (∑ b : α, if a = b then 0 else M₂.effect b) := by
     intro a
     rw [ProjectiveSetting.place_finsetSum, Finset.mul_sum]
     refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
     by_cases h : a = b
     · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, ProjectiveSetting.place_zero_local, mul_zero]
     · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]
   rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hrow a]
   refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => ?_
   exact ProjectiveSetting.place_mul_place_nonneg S p₁ p₂ hopp (M₁.pos a)
     (hcomplement a)

 by items 1 and 2 of blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
 `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`. -/
 theorem consistencyDefect_integrand_nonneg {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
     {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
     (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂)
     (M₁ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
     (M₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)) :
     0 ≤ ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
       if a = b then 0
       else (inner ℂ S.psiHat
         ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
             ℂ).symm
           ((S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)).mulVec
             S.psiHat))).re := by
   classical
   have hform : (∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
         if a = b then 0
         else (inner ℂ S.psiHat
           ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
               ℂ).symm
             ((S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)).mulVec
               S.psiHat))).re) =
       DistanceCalculus.stateQForm S.psiHat
         (∑ a : α, ∑ b : α, if a = b then 0
           else S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)) := by
     rw [DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_finset_sum]
     refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
     rw [DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_finset_sum]
     refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
     by_cases h : a = b
     · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, stateQForm_zero_local]
     · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]
       rfl
   rw [hform]

 /-!
 # Uniform collision bounds on nondegenerate affine lines
 
 This module combines uniqueness of affine evaluation with the univariate
 root-count bound to control collisions under a uniform line parameter.
 
 ## References
 
 The result is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
 `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
 -/
 
 namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
 
 open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
 
 noncomputable section
 
 /-- On a nondegenerate line, completed evaluations of distinct degree-bounded
 polynomials collide with probability at most the degree bound divided by the
 field size under a uniform affine parameter. -/
 theorem evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le {L : LdParams} {bound : ℕ}
     (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction ≠ 0)
     (first second : DegPoly L bound) (hne : first ≠ second) :
     avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
       if evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) first =
         evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) second then 1 else 0) ≤
       (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) := by
   classical
   simp_rw [evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero line hdir,
     Option.some.injEq]
   have hcard := evalCoefficient_collision_card_le first second hne
   unfold avgOver
   simp only [uniformDistribution_support, uniformDistribution_weight_apply,
     mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero, ← Finset.sum_filter]
   rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one_div]
   exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hcard) (by positivity)
 
 end
 
 end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Points.Commutation
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# The sandwich POVM of the expanded point measurements
     5	
     6	The first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` combines the two expanded point
     7	measurements into the sandwich POVM
     8	`R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^{(Point,Z),z}_b M^{(Point,X),x}_a M^{(Point,Z),z}_b`.  The
     9	source forms it from the binary refinements; here it is formed directly with
    10	outcomes in `F_q × F_q`, which the Parseval transfer of
    11	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Commutation.lean` makes possible.  This file
    12	defines the POVM, proves that it is close to the ordered product
    13	`M^Z_b M^X_a` by the approximate commutation, and records the consistency of
    14	the ordered products across opposite register placements, which follows from
    15	the self-consistency of each factor.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `ProjectiveSetting.sandwichPoint`: the sandwich POVM.
    20	* `sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le`: closeness of the sandwich to the ordered
    21	  product on every placement, with the error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.
    22	* `ordered_cross_dist_le`: the ordered product on one placement is close to
    23	  the reversed ordered product on the opposite placement.
    24	
    25	## References
    26	
    27	Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-748`
    28	(the sandwich and display `eq:qld-r-2`), blueprint
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:803-960` (`lem:qld-4-10`); the
    30	route is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.
    31	-/
    32	
    33	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    34	
    35	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    36	
    37	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    38	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    39	
    40	noncomputable section
    41	
    42	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    43	
    44	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    45	
    46	/-- An expanded point effect is self-adjoint. -/
    47	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    48	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    49	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    50	    ((S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a)ᴴ = (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    51	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq
    52	
    53	/-- An expanded point effect is idempotent. -/
    54	theorem pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    55	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    56	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    57	    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
    58	      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
    59	  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isIdempotentElem.eq
    60	
    61	/-- The sandwich `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` is `(M^X_a M^Z_b)ᴴ (M^X_a M^Z_b)`. -/
    62	theorem sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    63	    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    64	    (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    65	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b =
    66	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b)ᴴ *
    67	        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b) := by
    68	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
    69	    pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _
    70	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b),
    71	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a)
    72	      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a), pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self,
    73	    ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
    74	
    75	/-- The sandwich effects resolve the identity. -/
    76	theorem sum_sandwich_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    77	    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    78	    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
    79	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
    80	          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
    81	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 = 1 := by
    82	  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
    83	  calc ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
    84	        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
    85	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b
    86	      = ∑ b : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b *
    87	          (∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a) *
    88	          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b := by
    89	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    90	        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
    91	    _ = 1 := by
    92	        simp_rw [(S.pointMeasExp side .X x).sum_eq_one, mul_one,
    93	          pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
    94	        exact (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).sum_eq_one

    97	point measurements, with outcomes in `F_q × F_q`.  This is the POVM of the
    98	first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-736`,

    21	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) : Distribution (α × β) where
    22	  support := μ.support.product ν.support

    37	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
    38	    (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hν : ν.IsProbability) :
    39	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).IsProbability := by
    40	  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    41	    Distribution.prod]
    42	  calc
    43	    (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support, μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) =
    44	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, ∑ b ∈ ν.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b := by
    45	      exact Finset.sum_product' μ.support ν.support
    46	        (fun a b => μ.weight a * ν.weight b)
    47	    _ =
    48	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ∑ b ∈ ν.support, ν.weight b := by
    49	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    50	      intro a _
    51	      exact (Finset.mul_sum ν.support (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm
    52	    _ = ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a := by
    53	      rw [hν.weight_sum_eq_one]

    55	    _ = 1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one

    91	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a * c) = avgOver 𝒟 f * c := by
    92	  unfold avgOver
    93	  calc
    94	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * (f a * c)
    95	      = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, (𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by
    96	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    97	          intro a _
    98	          ring
    99	    _ = (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a) * c := by
   100	          rw [Finset.sum_mul]

   102	/-- Pull a finite outcome sum through an average. -/
   103	theorem avgOver_sum {α β : Type*} [Fintype β]
   104	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β → Error) :
   105	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ∑ b : β, f a b) =
   106	      ∑ b : β, avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a b) := by
   107	  rw [show (fun a => ∑ b : β, f a b) = ∑ b : β, fun a => f a b by
   108	    ext a
   109	    simp]
   110	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap]
   111	
   112	/-- Pull a finite-set sum through an average. -/
   113	theorem avgOver_finset_sum {α β : Type*}
   114	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (s : Finset β) (f : α → β → Error) :
   115	    avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => ∑ b ∈ s, f a b) =
   116	      ∑ b ∈ s, avgOver 𝒟 (fun a => f a b) := by
   117	  rw [show (fun a => ∑ b ∈ s, f a b) = ∑ b ∈ s, fun a => f a b by
   118	    ext a
   119	    simp]
   120	  simp [Distribution.avgOver_eq_weightedSumLinearMap]
   121	
   122	/-- Fubini swap for two nested finite-support distribution averages. -/
   123	theorem avgOver_comm {α β : Type*} (𝒟α : Distribution α) (𝒟β : Distribution β)
   124	    (f : α → β → Error) :
   125	    avgOver 𝒟α (fun a => avgOver 𝒟β (f a)) =
   126	      avgOver 𝒟β (fun b => avgOver 𝒟α (fun a => f a b)) := by
   127	  unfold avgOver
   128	  simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   129	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   130	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   131	  intro b _
   132	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   133	  intro a _
   134	  ring

   136	/-- If `f = g` pointwise, their averages agree. -/
   137	theorem avgOver_congr {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   138	    (f g : α → Error) (h : ∀ a, f a = g a) :
   139	    avgOver 𝒟 f = avgOver 𝒟 g := by
   140	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by rw [h a]

   143	averages agree.  This support-restricted form is useful for distributions whose
   144	support carries an invariant not available for all ambient values. -/

   146	    (f g : α → Error) (h : ∀ a, a ∈ 𝒟.support → f a = g a) :
   147	    avgOver 𝒟 f = avgOver 𝒟 g := by
   148	  simp only [avgOver]
   149	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => by rw [h a ha]

# Lean Proof Integrity Rules

This file is the **single source of truth** for proof integrity checks in this
repository. All CI workflows and review prompts should reference this file
rather than duplicating the rules inline.

> **Lean version**: 4.x (Lean 3 keywords like `constant` do not apply)

> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check below yet still
> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
> Consult it alongside this file during review.

> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
> blocker below may be temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
> conditional helper
> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.

---

## Blockers

These patterns **must** be resolved before merging.

### Direct proof holes

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `sorry` | Axiomatically closes any goal — the proof is incomplete |
| `admit` | Tactic alias for `sorry` |

### Kernel / type system bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `native_decide` | Relies on trusted native evaluation / compiler; banned in Mathlib for soundness and process reasons |
| `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce` | Type system bypass — can fabricate any proof term |
| `lcProof` | Low-level proof fabrication primitive — can prove `False` |
| `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat` | Kernel reduction primitives exploitable for unsound proofs |

### Axiom smuggling

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `axiom` declarations | Introduces unproven assumptions that could be inconsistent; must be explicitly justified |

When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
the axiomatic base.

This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
faithful to the paper.

### Circular reasoning

Lean's kernel forbids literal declaration cycles, so focus on **mathematical
circularity**:

- Proofs that assume (or trivially reintroduce) the statement being proved as a
  local hypothesis, then immediately close the goal from that hypothesis
- Helper lemmas in the same file that essentially restate the main goal and are
  only used to prove that goal
- Local `have`/`let` bindings that are just the goal rephrased, used to solve
  the goal without any real argument
- Newly introduced `axiom` that makes a difficult statement trivially provable
  without connecting to existing Mathlib / core theorems
- Abuse of `unsafe` features to fabricate proofs instead of giving a genuine
  derivation
- `by exact h` where `h` came from an unjustified assumption identical to the
  goal

### Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)

Proofs that avoid grounding in Mathlib:

- Custom re-declarations of standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., re-proving
  `add_comm` instead of importing it)
- `axiom` or `sorry`-based helper lemmas for facts that already exist in
  Mathlib
- Chains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core
- `private` helper lemmas that duplicate Mathlib API (e.g., custom matrix
  transpose lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)
- Overly long proof chains replaceable by a single Mathlib lemma

When flagging, perform an actual lookup (grep, `#find?`, `exact?`,
`library_search`). If an equivalent exists, cite the Mathlib lemma and module
path. If not, state "no equivalent found" with search evidence.

### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization

This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.

Signs to watch for:

- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
  incompatible universes)

When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
progress rather than enabling it.

### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift

A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
documented mathematical necessity.

The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.

Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.

Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.

Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
step of the source proof.

For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:

- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.

---

## Warnings

These should be flagged for review but may be acceptable with justification.

### Placeholder tactics

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`, `suggest` | Search tactics left as placeholders — replace with the concrete result |

### Safety / termination bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `unsafe def` | Bypasses Lean safety checks; should not appear in proof-relevant code |
| `partial def` | No termination proof required; unsound if used to build proof terms |
| `implemented_by` / `implementedBy` | Decouples runtime behavior from proven specification |

### Suspicious options

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `set_option maxHeartbeats 0` | Disables timeout — can hide non-terminating proofs |
| `set_option maxHeartbeats` with values >= 4,000,000 | 20x the default (200,000) — likely indicates an inefficient proof |
| `set_option maxRecDepth` with values >= 10,000 | May hide structural issues in proofs |

### Debug artifacts

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `dbg_trace` | Debug trace left in code |
| `stop` | Halts elaboration — development aid only |
| `#check`, `#eval`, `#print` in proof files | Debug commands that should be removed |

---

## How to use this file

**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.

**In CI review prompts**: Reference this file instead of inlining the rules:
```
Read `docs/PROOF_INTEGRITY.md` for the complete list of proof integrity
rules. Flag blockers as must-fix issues that should block merge.
Flag warnings as advisory — note them but acknowledge they may be
acceptable with justification.
```

**For manual review**: Use this as a checklist when reviewing Lean PRs.

**Updating rules**: Edit this file and all referencing workflows will
automatically pick up the changes.
# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns

Catalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks
(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to
prove the claimed mathematics. Complements
the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level
blockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the
trick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions
bake in*.

Every pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a
paper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all
cross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.

## Why this matters

Kernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:

- Be marked `\leanok` in the blueprint,
- Have a sorry-free proof body,
- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),

and still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof
obligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel
branch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this
codebase.

## Catalogue

- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)
- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)
- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)
- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)
- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)
- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)

---

## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis

**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own
conclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body
is a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no
mathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle
(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the
catalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by
PR [#491].

### Why it's bad

The theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;
the caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the
caller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the
stack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\leanok` tag
misrepresents the actual state of the proof.

### How to spot it

- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's
  conclusion.
- The proof body is one of:
  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`
  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`
  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`
- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,
  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.
- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).

### Concrete example

Historical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):

```lean
theorem mainInduction
    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)
    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :
    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,
      ConsRel strategy.state ...
        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by
  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩
  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩
  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩
```

Here `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type
`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally
the conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this
specific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed
the same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains
the archetypal example of the anti-pattern.

PR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's
fields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across
individual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse
because the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs
that discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped
existential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name
that suggests the paper result has been proved.

### How to fix it

Prefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses
— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's
conclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content
cannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation
to be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open
under a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as
an extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof
debt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not
the preferred shape for new work.

A signature passes the smell test if:

- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the
  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and
- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*
  theorem, not a trivially-false one.

### Related issues and patterns

- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker
- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue
- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by
  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly
- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)
- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern
- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation

---

## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand

**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and
a nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line
`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The "mathematical
content" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See
issues [#477], [#494].

### Why it's bad

`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen
*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` "proof" transports none of the
paper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to
match the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,
`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated
anywhere in Lean.

### How to spot it

- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where
  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.
- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a
  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a
  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.
- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting
  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.
- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function
  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field
  directly.

### Concrete example

From `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:

```lean
/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/
def fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)
    (α β : Point params) : Error :=
  if α = β then 1 else 0

/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/
lemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)
    (α β : Point params) :
    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl

/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/
theorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :
    (∀ α β : Point params,
      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro α β
    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta
  ...
```

The paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an
orthonormal basis under the actual inner product
`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum
identity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the
definition equals itself.

### Not every `rfl` is a castle

Distinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally
how something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in
`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of
`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is
elsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is
a naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper
identity, or does it just name a compound expression?**

### How to fix it

1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define
   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters
   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.
2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those
   concrete objects.
3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib
   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`
   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).
4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a
   consequence, not as the primitive.

### Related issues

- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)
- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates

---

## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions

**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else
default`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or
`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for "precondition not met." Downstream
theorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the
theorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the
obligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the
function. See issue [#495], related to [#307].

### Why it's bad

The signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a
non-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about "the output" is
proved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a
later theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition
type-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original
precondition failed.

The paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:
"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`." The Lean should
match.

### How to spot it

- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.
- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.
- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,
  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.
- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.
- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial
  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.

### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)

Until PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:

```lean
/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/
noncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=
  match g with
  | some p => p.poly
  | none   => 0
```

The consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange
interpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained
a `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.
The paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the
Lean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead
it carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for
which its conclusion was meaningless.

**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,
threads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into
`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset
# Proof Frontier Review

This document gives a checklist for reviewing Lean changes that introduce or
thread structure fields in the formalization. Its purpose is to prevent a
well-typed bookkeeping layer from being mistaken for a mathematical construction
theorem.

The central distinction is this:

- An **obligation discharger** derives a mathematical object or relation from
  the hypotheses appearing in the paper or blueprint.
- An **external residual** records a missing obligation discharger explicitly,
  with a named issue and a statement of the mathematical obstruction.
- A **bookkeeping conversion** changes the form or namespace of an already
  available object without deriving a new mathematical fact.

All three forms can be legitimate. The review problem is to identify which one
has been added, and to make sure the prose, blueprint tags, and issue status say
the same thing.

## Why Source-Level Holes Are Not Enough

The number of occurrences of `sorry` in the source is only a kernel-level
metric. It does not determine the mathematical frontier. A proof can be
`sorry`-free while still assuming the object that the paper asks one to
construct, for example by adding a field to a structure and proving the next
theorem by projecting that field.

For the LDT development this distinction matters most near the main theorem,
the main induction step, self-improvement, orthonormalization, and
projectivization. In these regions, a single displayed statement in the paper
usually depends on several intermediate constructions. Closing one local source
hole may only move the remaining obligation into an input structure.

## Reviewer Checklist

Before approving a PR that adds or modifies a structure field in a type named
with a suffix such as `Input`, `Residual`, `BridgeInputs`, `Witness`,
`Statement`, `Conclusion`, or `Obligations`, check the following points.

1. **Classify each new field.** State whether the field is produced in the PR,
   remains an external residual, or is only a bookkeeping conversion.
2. **Name the obligation discharger.** If the field is produced, cite the exact
   Lean theorem that derives it from the paper hypotheses. If no such theorem
   exists, keep the parent mathematical issue open and link a native sub-issue
   for the missing obligation.
3. **Check the blueprint frontier.** For work near `mainFormal`, Section 6,
   self-improvement, orthonormalization, or projectivization, inspect
   `blueprint/dep_graph_document.html` after building the blueprint. The
   remaining open vertices are part of the review context, even when the source
   diff contains no `sorry`.
4. **Reject hidden residual drift.** A theorem that merely moves an assumption
   into a structure field should be described as a conditional helper or a
   remaining obligation, not as proving the paper step.
5. **Review public prose.** Docstrings, module text, PR descriptions, and
   blueprint paragraphs should distinguish obligations proved from the paper
   hypotheses from inputs of conditional helpers and bookkeeping conversions.
6. **Size follow-up tasks by proof leaves.** Prefer issues such as "prove the
   raw Step 3 Cauchy--Schwarz estimate" to issues such as "close the
   self-improvement inputs" when the latter contains several independent
   proof obligations.
7. **Use native sub-issues.** Missing obligations should be linked under the
   correct parent tracker instead of being left only in a PR comment.

## Diagonal and Completion Data

The recent Section 6 and self-improvement work exposed several tracked
proof-obligation structures. They should be reviewed as debt to remove, not as
new source hypotheses to normalize. The recurring ambiguity is that a theorem
may mention diagonal data, completion data, or restricted strategy data while
only repackaging such data as an explicit input.

For any theorem whose name or docstring mentions diagonal consistency,
line-130 data, completion, restricted strategies, or repaired strategy data,
reviewers should ask the following mathematical question:

Does the theorem derive the stated object from the paper hypotheses, or does it
assume that object as a field?

For line 130 of `references/ldt-paper/inductive_step.tex`, in particular,
the paper supplies a cross relation between `G^A` and `G^B`. A Lean theorem
that consumes diagonal strong self-consistency of `G^A` or `G^B` should not be
described as deriving that diagonal input unless it contains the missing
argument.

## Blueprint Tags

Use `\leanok` only when the Lean declaration proves the mathematical assertion
of the blueprint node under the stated hypotheses. If the Lean declaration is a
conditional wrapper or input splitter, then the blueprint should say so
explicitly. It may still cite the declaration with `\lean{...}`, but the prose
must identify the remaining obligation.

When a PR introduces a public auxiliary lemma that is not a named paper
statement, the blueprint should either omit it or cite it as a subordinate
formalization-only support lemma. Do not allow a support lemma to inherit the
status of the paper theorem whose proof will eventually consume it.

## Examples From the Project

- Issue #1110 and the surrounding Section 6 work showed that diagonal and
  line-130 inputs can be made type-correct without proving the diagonal
  obligation. Such declarations must be described as conditional inputs.
- Issue #1109 concerned final-field boundedness. The generalized theorem
  `final_fields_bounded` is a genuine obligation discharger once the SDP dual
  witness satisfies `I <= Z`; the blueprint prose was updated to state that
  hypothesis and the theorem's actual generality.
- Issues #1070 and #1072 are examples of proof-frontier work where individual
  structure fields had to be separated from the mathematical obligation still
  tracked by the parent self-improvement issue.
- Issue #1081 and parent issue #931 illustrate why a parent tracker should stay
  open when a PR only supplies a conditional helper or residual record.

These examples are not special exceptions. They are the model for future review:
identify the mathematical obligation, name the residual when it remains, and
keep the public prose faithful to that distinction.

nodes to blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex —
lem:qld-completed-point-answers, lem:qld-completed-point-self-consistency and
lem:qld-conditioned-completed-point-self-consistency. Each displays its own
question law and error bound: the product line-point law with error delta_Q,
and the law conditioned on a nonzero first-line direction with error
delta_Q divided by the retained mass. The conditioned node is stated as a
formalization-only restriction and is not linked to the source-labelled
eq:pasting-2.

F2 (prose, answer ordering): the X-Z-X sandwich reads as a pasting instance
with inner family the Z-line family and outer family the X-line family
(ProjectiveSetting.combinedLineMeasurement_effect_eq_pastedMeasurement), so
the pasted answer pair is ordered Z then X, as in the conditioned marginal
comparisons of ConditionedPointLineMarginalDefect. Add
CombinedPointsWitness.completed_orderedZX_effect and the two Z-then-X
estimates self_consistency_completed_orderedZX_linePoint_defect_le and
self_consistency_conditioned_completed_orderedZX_defect_le, proved from the
existing X-then-Z estimates by consistencyDefect_outcome_equiv along
Equiv.prodComm; the module reference paragraph now states the ordering
instead of claiming the printed premise.

F3 (prose, traceability status): every public declaration of the module now
has a blueprint entry with \lean, \leanok and \uses tags; the generated,
git-ignored blueprint/lean_decls index was regenerated accordingly. No
\leanok was added to the source lemma lem:qld-xz-lines, whose \notready
remains.

mathematical prose. "Completing with some" becomes "extending along the
coordinatewise inclusion into the completed answer alphabet", and the
"proof-only nondegenerate pasting question law" becomes "the product
line-point distribution conditioned on a nonzero direction of the first
line".

dispositioned the Extraction/Consistency.lean placement and

here.

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditional collision bounds from fiber averages
     5	
     6	This module converts an unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question
     7	fiber into the positive-mass conditional collision predicate used by the
     8	pasting theorem.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The conditional collision hypothesis is from `lem:pasting`,
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. Its use in
    14	the QPBT combining argument occurs at
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`.
    16	-/

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	/-- An unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question fiber implies
    27	the positive-mass conditional collision predicate of `lem:pasting`. This is a
    28	formalization-only normalization adapter for paper lines 504--525. -/
    29	theorem collision_bound_of_fiber_averages {X Y₁ Y₂ R₂ Γ₂ : Type*}
    30	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]
    31	    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]
    32	    [Fintype Γ₂] (dist : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂))
    33	    (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂) (eta : ℝ)
    34	    (hbound : ∀ fixed : X × Y₁, ∀ first second : Γ₂, first ≠ second →
    35	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then
    36	        (if eval₂ first sample.2 = eval₂ second sample.2 then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    37	      eta * avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then 1 else 0)) :
    38	    HasConditionalCollisionBound dist eval₂ eta := by
    39	  classical
    40	  intro question point _ first second hne
    41	  have havg (value : ((X × Y₁) × Y₂) → ℝ) :
    42	      avgOver dist value = ∑ sample, dist.weight sample * value sample := by
    43	    exact (dist.sum_univ_eq_sum_support _ (fun sample hout => by
    44	      rw [dist.outsideSupport sample hout, zero_mul])).symm
    45	  have hmass : (dist.map Prod.fst).weight (question, point) =
    46	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = (question, point) then 1 else 0) := by
    47	    rw [Distribution.map_weight]
    48	    unfold avgOver
    49	    rw [Finset.sum_filter]
    50	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    51	    intro sample _
    52	    by_cases hfixed : sample.1 = (question, point) <;> simp [hfixed]
    53	  rw [hmass]
    54	  have h := hbound (question, point) first second hne
    55	  simpa [havg, Fintype.sum_prod_type, mul_ite] using h
    56	
    57	end
    58	
    59	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    27	        (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)).support.filter

    34	on nonzero first-line direction and relabeling the two samples for pasting. -/
    35	def nondegenerateLinePastingDist (L : LdParams) :
    36	    Distribution (((LineDesc L × LineDesc L) ×
    37	      (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) ×
    38	        (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))) :=
    39	  (Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L))

    42	      (fun samples => (((samples.1.1, samples.2.1), samples.2), samples.1))

    46	    (nondegenerateLinePastingDist L).IsProbability := by
    47	  exact (Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
    48	    (prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_mass_pos L)).map _

   428	\subsection*{Use analysis}
   429	
   430	A search of both paper mirrors finds one direct application of
   431	\texttt{lem:pasting} in the QPBT paper, in the proof of
   432	\texttt{lem:qld-xz-lines}, lines~938--962 of
   433	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}.
   434	There $A=\hat Q$, the two codeword families are the expanded line
   435	measurements, and the collision bound is $md/q$ by Schwartz--Zippel.
   436	The displayed assignment of $G_1,G_2$ in the source reverses the order of its
   437	displayed sandwich $T=M_XM_ZM_X$. To obtain precisely that $T$, take $G_1=M_Z$,
   438	$G_2=M_X$, and exchange the two answer coordinates in $A$ and in the final
   439	postprocessing. Both line families are projective and the same conditional
   440	Schwartz--Zippel bound holds with the roles exchanged. This is an application
   441	and outcome relabelling, not a change to the definition of $T$.
   442	The input comparisons come from \texttt{lem:qld-4-10}; that lemma is an
   443	\emph{input}, not a consequence of pasting. Its symmetric equivalents also
   444	permit the conditional theorem at this application, but do not establish a
   445	symmetric domain for the general operator lemma. The mirror proof leaves
   446	$J$ unchanged, so the definition of the joint line measurement $T$ and every
   447	subsequent use of its consistency, positivity, and completeness are unchanged.
   448	
   449	This is one direct application, not a single dependent theorem. The
   450	\texttt{lem:qld-xz-lines} conclusion is used for restricted line laws, for
   451	the combined line construction following \texttt{lem:qld-sublines}, and for
   452	the three consistency calculations leading to \texttt{lem:qld-4-13} and
   453	\texttt{lem:qld-4-7}. The extraction construction then uses the resulting
   454	combined measurement, through \texttt{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} and
   455	\texttt{lem:qld-unitary}, ending at the proof of
   456	\texttt{thm:pauli-appendix}, lines~1862--1876 of the same source file.
   457	These uses require only the same joint measurement,
   458	the same directed comparisons, and an unspecified universal polynomial-small
   459	error. Replacing that error by a sum of positive powers, and then composing
   460	with $\delta_Q$, remains a sum of positive powers. No use requires the
   461	particular exponents of the conditional proof.

   130	
   131	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   132	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   133	order
   134	\[
   135	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   136	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   137	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   138	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   139	\]
   140	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   141	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   142	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   143	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   144	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   145	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   146	
   147	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   148	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   149	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   150	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   151	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   152	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   153	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   154	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   155	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   156	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   157	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   158	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   159	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   160	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   161	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   162	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   163	
   164	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   165	\[
   166	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   167	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   168	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   169	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   170	\]
   171	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   172	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   173	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   174	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.

   176	The remaining construction target is
   177	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   178	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it asks for evaluated consistency
   179	of the explicit unconditioned measurement

   181	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   182	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   183	\]
   184	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   185	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite

   187	pasting argument at lines 942--961 are the intended discharge. The POVM,

   189	
   190	A bound for a measurement conditioned on nondegenerate lines would not by
   191	itself discharge this target. It would also require a defined conditioning
   192	event, its probability, an estimate for the discarded contribution, and a
   193	transfer of the defect back to the unconditioned measurement above under the
   194	original product law. No such transfer is asserted here. In particular,
   195	the preserved conditioned construction is not identified with

   197	The current target retains its explicit unfinished proof, without assuming

   200	\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}
   201	
   202	The same quantitative omission remains in the auxiliary
   203	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
   204	function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
   205	at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does
   228	 Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
   229	 \begin{cases}
   230	   \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
   231	   0,&\text{otherwise}.
   232	 \end{cases}
   233	\]
   234	This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
   235	every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
   236	two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
   237	maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
   238	point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.
   239	
   240	The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
   241	indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
   242	of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
   243	On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
   244	in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
   245	parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
   246	has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
   247	two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
   248	most $2/q$.
   249	
   250	This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
   251	be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
   252	player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and
   253	$\sum_p w_p=1$; the axis-degree field makes $w_p=0$ for higher-degree answers.
   254	The opposite point effect is deterministically the identity at $\alpha x^2$,
   255	so the agreement is precisely the $w_p$-weighted average of those root-count
   256	fractions. These weights depend on the line but not on $x$ along it. Averaging
   257	over the fixed coordinates, and using nonnegativity of the defect on the
   258	remaining question branches, gives for either player orientation
   259	\[
   260	 \operatorname{defect}\ \ge\
   261	 \frac18\left(1-\frac1q\right)\left(1-\frac2q\right).
   262	\]
   263	There is no undefined evaluation on these nonzero axis directions, so the
   264	completed answer alphabet does not change this calculation. The scalar field
   265	identification preserves the polynomial evaluations and their root counts.
   266	
   267	The lower bound tends to $1/8$. In contrast, the predicate
   268	\path{IsPolyErr}\textsubscript{2} bounds the proposed error at these parameters by
   269	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(0,1/q)\le Cq^{-s}$ with $s>0$, which tends to zero.
   270	For the first-route estimate, the polynomial-error bound on $g$ likewise gives
   271	fixed constants $K\ge1$ and $r,s>0$ with
   272	$C g(0,1/q)\le CKq^{-s}\longrightarrow0$.
   273	Consequently both unrestricted supplied-point auxiliaries are false,
   274	independently of the printed-error discrepancy and the diagonal-line degeneracy.
   275	This argument does not refute the existential point-witness declarations or the source
   276	\path{lem:qld-4-13}; neither requires a line approximation to every arbitrarily
   277	chosen point family.
   278	
   279	Two parts of the obstruction are independently verified in Lean: every
   280	projective joint family admits some finite witness error, and a coefficient
   281	answer with zero quadratic coefficient agrees with a nonzero multiple of the
   282	square function with probability at most $2/q$.\footnote{The declarations are
   283	\path{CombinedPointsWitness.exists_error_of_projective} and
   284	\path{linear_quadratic_agreement_le} in
   285	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/PointErrorObstruction.lean}. The first uses the
   286	existence of an upper bound for a finite set of real numbers; the second reuses
   287	\path{directCoefficientCollision_avg_le}, which reduces to Mathlib's
   288	univariate root count. The complete strategy-level contradiction is the
   289	mathematical argument above, not a Lean counterexample theorem: the formal
   290	perfect-strategy construction and the formal integration of the lower bound
   291	remain to be supplied.}
   292	The existing auxiliary signatures and their unfinished proofs are preserved
   293	pending a separately scoped repair. A source-faithful existence proof must
   294	construct polynomially controlled points internally and retain their error
   295	through the line estimates; it cannot cover arbitrary supplied point
   296	measurements by discarding their error parameter. Even after that domain
   297	repair, the separate printed-error estimate discussed below remains open.

     4	/-!
     5	# Diagonal line-point parameter resampling
     6	
     7	This module proves that a uniform affine parameter may replace the sampled
     8	point on a diagonal line without changing the joint diagonal line-point law,
     9	including its zero-direction fibers.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The result supports the Schwartz-Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`, for
    15	the diagonal sampler of
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- Resampling a uniform parameter on the sampled diagonal line preserves the
    26	joint line-point law, including the zero-direction fibers. This
    27	formalization-only identity derives the conditional sampling used at paper
    28	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:955` from `def:line-point-dist`. -/
    29	theorem avgOver_dLinePointDist_resample_parameter (L : LdParams)
    30	    (value : (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)) -> ℝ) :
    31	    avgOver (dLinePointDist L) value =
    32	      avgOver (dLinePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    33	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    34	          value (sample.1, sample.1.base + param • sample.1.direction))) := by
    35	  classical
    36	  unfold dLinePointDist clDistribution
    37	  simp only [Distribution.avgOver_map, dLineDescOf_ldDLineCL]
    38	  have hblock := uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm
    39	  rw [← hblock]
    40	  simp only [Distribution.avgOver_map]
    41	  rw [uniformDistribution_prod]
    42	  simp only [avgOver_prod]
    43	  rw [avgOver_comm, avgOver_comm (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L))]
    44	  apply congrArg
    45	  funext block
    46	  let direction : Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L :=
    47	    prefixProjection (chiIndex L block.1) block.2
    48	  have hprefix : ∀ index : Fin L.m, index.val < (chiIndex L block.1).val ->
    49	      direction index = 0 := by
    50	    intro index hindex
    51	    simp [direction, prefixProjection, hindex]
    52	  have hresample (direction : Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)
    53	      (quantity : (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L) ->
    54	        (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L) -> ℝ) :
    55	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L))
    56	          (fun point => quantity (lineRepMap direction point) point) =
    57	        avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    58	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    59	            quantity (lineRepMap direction point)
    60	              (lineRepMap direction point + param • direction))) := by
    61	    have hmap := uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul direction
    62	    have havg := congrArg (fun dist => avgOver dist
    63	      (fun point => quantity (lineRepMap direction point) point)) hmap
    64	    rw [Distribution.avgOver_map, uniformDistribution_prod, avgOver_prod] at havg
    65	    simpa only [lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self] using havg.symm
    66	  change avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    67	      value (LineDesc.diagonal (lineRepMap direction point) block.1 direction
    68	        (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point) hprefix, point)) =
    69	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m -> ScalarQ L)) (fun point =>
    70	      avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    71	        value (LineDesc.diagonal (lineRepMap direction point) block.1 direction
    72	          (lineRepMap_apply_self direction point) hprefix,
    73	          lineRepMap direction point + param • direction)))
    74	  have h := hresample direction
    75	    (fun base point => value (LineDesc.diagonal
    76	      (lineRepMap direction base) block.1 direction
    77	      (lineRepMap_apply_self direction base) hprefix, point))
    78	  simpa only [lineRepMap_apply_self] using h
    79	
    80	end
    81	
    82	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Evaluation on a nondegenerate affine line
     5	
     6	This module identifies completed line-polynomial evaluation with evaluation at
     7	the unique affine parameter of a point on a line with nonzero direction.
     8	
     9	## References

    11	The result is the geometric step in the collision argument at
    12	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.

    19	noncomputable section
    20	
    21	/-- On a nonzero direction, completed evaluation agrees with polynomial
    22	evaluation at the unique affine parameter. -/
    23	theorem evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero {L : LdParams}
    24	    {bound : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction ≠ 0)
    25	    (poly : DegPoly L bound) (param : ScalarQ L) :
    26	    evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) poly =
    27	      some (evalCoefficient poly param) := by
    28	  apply WinImplications.evalOpt_eq_some_of_evaluatesTo
    29	  refine ⟨⟨param, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    30	  intro other heq
    31	  have hsmul : param • line.direction = other • line.direction :=
    32	    add_left_cancel heq
    33	  have hsub : (param - other) • line.direction = 0 := by
    34	    rw [sub_smul, hsmul, sub_self]
    35	  have hparam : param = other :=
    36	    sub_eq_zero.mp ((smul_eq_zero.mp hsub).resolve_right hdir)
    37	  rw [hparam]
    38	
    39	end
    40	
    41	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Uniform collision bounds on nondegenerate affine lines
     6	
     7	This module combines uniqueness of affine evaluation with the univariate
     8	root-count bound to control collisions under a uniform line parameter.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The result is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    17	
    18	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    19	
    20	noncomputable section
    21	
    22	/-- On a nondegenerate line, completed evaluations of distinct degree-bounded
    23	polynomials collide with probability at most the degree bound divided by the
    24	field size under a uniform affine parameter. -/
    25	theorem evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le {L : LdParams} {bound : ℕ}
    26	    (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction ≠ 0)
    27	    (first second : DegPoly L bound) (hne : first ≠ second) :
    28	    avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
    29	      if evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) first =
    30	        evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) second then 1 else 0) ≤
    31	      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) := by
    32	  classical
    33	  simp_rw [evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero line hdir,
    34	    Option.some.injEq]
    35	  have hcard := evalCoefficient_collision_card_le first second hne
    36	  unfold avgOver
    37	  simp only [uniformDistribution_support, uniformDistribution_weight_apply,
    38	    mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero, ← Finset.sum_filter]
    39	  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one_div]
    40	  exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hcard) (by positivity)
    41	
    42	end
    43	
    44	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Weighted collision bounds for sampled lines
     6	
     7	This module lifts the uniform affine-parameter collision estimate to the mixed
     8	line-point distribution with an arbitrary nonnegative weight depending only on
     9	the sampled line.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The estimate is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	noncomputable section
    22	
    23	/-- The collision bound remains valid with any nonnegative weight depending
    24	only on the line, after restricting to nonzero directions. This proof-only
    25	estimate is the conditional form of the root argument in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    26	paper lines 950--955; it does not assert the false unrestricted collision bound
    27	on zero-direction coefficient presentations. -/
    28	theorem linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le {L : LdParams}
    29	    {bound : ℕ} (weight : LineDesc L → ℝ)
    30	    (hweight : ∀ line, 0 ≤ weight line) (first second : DegPoly L bound)
    31	    (hne : first ≠ second) :
    32	    avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    33	      if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight sample.1 *
    34	        (if evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 first = evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 second
    35	          then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    36	      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) *
    37	        avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    38	          if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight sample.1 else 0) := by
    39	  classical
    40	  rw [avgOver_linePointDist_resample_parameter]
    41	  rw [← avgOver_const_mul]
    42	  apply avgOver_mono
    43	  intro sample
    44	  by_cases hdir : sample.1.direction ≠ 0
    45	  · simp only [if_pos hdir]
    46	    rw [avgOver_const_mul]
    47	    exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    48	      (evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le sample.1 hdir first second hne)
    49	      (hweight sample.1)).trans_eq
    50	      (mul_comm _ _)
    51	  · simp [hdir, avgOver]
    52	
    53	end
    54	
    55	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Product-distribution weighted collision bounds
     6	
     7	This module lifts the nondegenerate weighted collision estimate for one
     8	line-point sample to two independent samples. The nonnegative weight may
     9	depend on the complete second sample and on the first sampled line.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	This is formalization-only conditioning support for `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`, using
    15	the collision hypothesis of `lem:pasting` at
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- Independent sampling of a second line-point pair preserves the weighted
    26	collision estimate on nonzero first directions. The weight may depend on the
    27	complete second sample, but on the first sample only through its line. No
    28	condition is imposed on the second direction. -/
    29	theorem prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le
    30	    {L : LdParams} {bound : ℕ}
    31	    (weight : LineDesc L → (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) → ℝ)
    32	    (hweight : ∀ line sample, 0 ≤ weight line sample)
    33	    (first second : DegPoly L bound) (hne : first ≠ second) :
    34	    avgOver (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)) (fun samples =>
    35	      if samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight samples.1.1 samples.2 *
    36	        (if evalOpt samples.1.1 samples.1.2 first =
    37	          evalOpt samples.1.1 samples.1.2 second then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    38	    (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) *
    39	      avgOver (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)) (fun samples =>
    40	        if samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight samples.1.1 samples.2 else 0) := by
    41	  classical
    42	  simp only [avgOver_prod]
    43	  rw [avgOver_comm, avgOver_comm (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)
    44	    (fun firstSample secondSample =>
    45	      if firstSample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight firstSample.1 secondSample else 0)]
    46	  rw [← avgOver_const_mul]
    47	  apply avgOver_mono
    48	  intro sample
    49	  exact linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le
    50	    (fun line => weight line sample) (fun line => hweight line sample)
    51	    first second hne
    52	
    53	end
    54	
    55	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
